differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar separates brokers from storage (BookKeeper), enabling independent scaling of compute and storage, ideal for varied workloads and long-term retention.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka uses brokers that also manage storage, leading to tighter coupling. Scaling storage often means scaling brokers, which can be less flexible.

differences.title: 2. CONSUMPTION MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar offers multiple subscription types (Exclusive, Shared, Failover, Key_Shared) for diverse consumption patterns, enhancing message delivery guarantees and ordering.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka's consumer groups provide load balancing and fault tolerance but offer less granular control over message ordering and delivery semantics.

differences.title: 3. MESSAGE PROCESSING
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar's architecture inherently supports strong multi-tenancy with isolation via namespaces and resource management, crucial for shared cloud environments.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka requires careful topic and partition management for isolation. Multi-tenancy often needs external tooling or careful configuration to achieve.

differences.title: 4. DATA REPLICATION
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar replicates data at the segment level using Apache BookKeeper, offering fine-grained fault tolerance and consistency guarantees across storage nodes.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka replicates entire topic partitions. This simpler model is highly performant but can lead to performance bottlenecks if partitions are unevenly loaded.

differences.title: 5. OPERATIONAL COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar's decoupled nature and built-in geo-replication simplify operations, especially in managing clusters across multiple data centers.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka traditionally relies on ZooKeeper for coordination, adding operational overhead. Managing partitions and broker configurations can be complex.

differences.title: 6. STREAMING CAPABILITIES
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar natively supports both traditional message queuing semantics and stream processing, making it versatile for various application patterns.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka excels at high-throughput event streaming and log aggregation. Adapting it for traditional queuing requires more effort and specific patterns.

differences.title: 7. CLOUD NATIVE DESIGN
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar's tiered storage allows offloading older data to cheaper cloud storage (S3, GCS), optimizing cost and simplifying capacity planning.
differences.rightDesc: Kafka's design prioritizes performance by keeping data on local disks within brokers. Cloud-native features often require external integrations.
